newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen kill Algerian official; new massacre reported.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Algerian official; new massacre reported.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead the deputy leader of an appointed local council in Algiers on Thursday night, 24 hours after five people were killed by presumed Moslem fundamentalists in another suburb, residents said on Friday.
"The deputy president of the communal executive council was assassinated by gunmen around 8 p.m. (1900 GMT) on Thursday near his office in Badjarrah," one resident said by telephone.
Another confirmed the killing of the official who was not named. Residents in Baraki, 12 km (eight miles) southeast of the capital, said five people had been killed overnight Wednesday to Thursday.
"Some were shot and others were stabbed to death," said one.

There has been no official confirmation of the killings or of an unconfirmed report circulating in Algiers that 22 people died after having their throats cut in Benhamdane, Blida province, during Wednesday night. Eight more were wounded.
Since early November about 400 people have been killed in attacks on villages, at fake road blocks, or by bombs in and around Algiers.
Moslem radicals have been fighting the authorities since early 1992 after they cancelled a general election Islamists were poised to win. About 60,000 people have died.
